calls.head: Strength against strength
calls.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Avalanche are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Stars’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Stars’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Avalanche.

calls.head: The Stars get in close, the Avalanche shoot from distance
calls.body: On shots from in close, Dallas is one of the league’s best, but Colorado is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Stars to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Avalanche edge the Stars
paras: Artturi Lehkonen opened the scoring for the Avalanche midway through the first, and Radek Faksa and Fedor Svechkov fought late in the period. Tyler Seguin tied it 1-1 for Dallas on the power play later in the period. Martin Nečas put the Avalanche ahead for good early in the second. Nathan MacKinnon and Roope Hintz dropped the gloves midway through the period. For MacKinnon, it was his second fight this season, after one in the four seasons before. Nečas struck again on the power play late in the period to make it 3-1 for the Avalanche, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Hintz pulled the Stars within one early in the third.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Mackenzie Blackwood made 24 saves for the Avalanche, and Jake Oettinger stopped 22 of 25. The Avs improved to 4-2-0, and the Stars dropped to 2-3-1.

items.text: Nathan MacKinnon extended his point streak against Dallas to eleven games.
With Wyatt Johnston out, Seguin took his spot and had a goal and an assist.
All three of the preview’s calls held.
